landing.heroBody: flashkarte is a spaced-repetition flashcard app. Write your cards in plain Markdown — or let your own AI build them — and it schedules each review for the moment right before you'd forget. Study on the web or on Android, always in sync.
landing.feature1Body: Write cards in plain Markdown — paste, import a file, or generate them. No clunky editors.
landing.feature2Body: A proven SM-2 schedule shows you each card right before you'd forget it, so reviews stay short.
landing.feature3Body: Web and Android, in sync. Pick up your reviews on the bus and finish them at your desk.
landing.feature4Body: Connect your own AI assistant over MCP to turn notes into decks — no extra subscription.

privacy.title: flashkarte — Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: flashkarte is a Markdown-based flashcard app with spaced-repetition study, operated by Christopher Rehm (Germany). This policy explains what data the app collects, why, and your choices. Questions or requests: <0>car2187bus@pm.me</0>.
privacy.collectAccount: <0>Account details</0> — your email address and a password. The password is never stored in plain text; only a salted hash is kept.
privacy.collectContent: <0>Your content</0> — the flashcard decks and cards you create or import, and your study progress (review history and scheduling).
privacy.collectApiKeys: <0>API keys</0> — if you generate a key to connect an AI client via the MCP server, we store a hashed form of that key (shown to you in full only once).
privacy.collectDiagnostics: <0>Diagnostic reports</0> — when the app hits an error it may send a report (error message, technical stack trace, app version, and platform) to our server log so we can fix bugs. These reports are used only for debugging.
privacy.dontAds: No advertising, no ad networks, and no third-party analytics or tracking.
privacy.dontSell: We do not sell or rent your personal data to anyone.
privacy.dontTrain: We do not use your decks or content to train any model.
privacy.aiBody: flashkarte lets you connect your own AI assistant (for example via Claude) through a hosted MCP server, using a personal API key, so the AI can create decks in your account. When you use that, requests are processed by <0>your own</0> AI provider under their terms and privacy policy — the AI computation does not run on our servers.
privacy.storageHeading: How your data is stored and protected
privacy.storageBody: Data is stored in a PostgreSQL database on a private server in the EU. All traffic to the service is encrypted with HTTPS (TLS). Passwords are hashed, and API keys are stored hashed. Backups of the database are kept on a rolling schedule and then deleted.
privacy.retentionBody: We keep your account data for as long as your account exists. You can delete individual decks at any time in the app. To delete your entire account and associated data, email <0>car2187bus@pm.me</0> from your account email address and we will remove it.
privacy.childrenBody: flashkarte is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect data from them.
privacy.rightsBody: Depending on where you live (for example under the EU GDPR), you may have the right to access, correct, export, or delete your personal data. Contact us at the address above to exercise these rights.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes, we will update the date at the top of this page.

guide.metaDescription: How to use flashkarte: write Markdown flashcard decks, study with spaced repetition, share decks, and let your AI build decks for you.
guide.title: How to use flashkarte
guide.intro: flashkarte turns plain Markdown into spaced-repetition flashcards you can study on the web and on Android, always in sync. This guide shows how to create and design decks, study them, share them, and connect an AI assistant.
guide.startBody: Sign up with an email and password, then confirm the verification email. Your decks and study progress are tied to your account and sync across every device you sign in on.
guide.createIntro: There are three ways to create a deck:
guide.createWeb: On the web, open the deck editor, paste or type Markdown in the format below, and save. A live preview shows the parsed cards before you save.
guide.createAndroid: In the Android app, create or import a deck the same way using the same Markdown format.
guide.createAI: Let an AI assistant build a deck for you — see Connect an AI assistant below.
guide.formatIntro: A deck is plain Markdown. The first heading is the title; an optional italic line under it is decorative and ignored. Use second-level headings to group cards into categories, and a line of dashes as a visual separator.
guide.formatCardsIntro: Write cards in either of two formats — you can mix both in one deck:
guide.formatBold: Numbered bold front: a bold line like "**1. front**" starts a card; the lines below it are the answer.
guide.formatQA: Q:/A: format: a "Q:" line is the front; the first "A:" line is the answer, and any lines after it become a second paragraph.
guide.formatParagraphs: Within an answer, consecutive lines join into one paragraph; leave a blank line to start a new paragraph.
guide.branchingBody: Turn a deck into a choose-your-path sequence. Put an anchor like "[label]" on its own line before a card, then give each option as a line "- choice text -> target", where target is another anchor label (or "end" to finish). A card with no options is a normal card.
guide.settingsOrdered: Study in order: when enabled, cards are shown in their authored order and you must answer the current card correctly before advancing — useful for sequences that build on each other.
guide.settingsPublic: Public decks: make a deck public to get a shareable page and have it listed on the Explore page, where anyone can preview it and clone it into their own account.
guide.studySrs: flashkarte schedules reviews with the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm, so cards you find hard come back sooner and easy ones later.
guide.studyRatings: In the default flip mode you reveal the answer and rate your recall — Again, Hard, Good, or Easy — which sets when the card is next due.
guide.studyChoice: The Android app also offers a multiple-choice mode that builds answer options automatically from your other cards and grades you on the tap.
guide.aiBody: An AI assistant can build decks for you and push them straight into your account, using your own AI account.
guide.aiStep1: In Settings, generate an API key and copy the MCP server URL.
guide.aiStep2: Add the URL as a custom connector in your AI client (for example claude.ai or Claude Desktop) and sign in with your flashkarte account.
guide.aiStep3: Ask it to build a deck, e.g. "Turn this into a flashkarte deck: …", and the new deck appears in your account.
